question.text: Ganga Resolution Fund (Cat I SSF) wants to bid as a Resolution Applicant in the CIRP of 'Yamuna Steel'. Under Chapter 9's SSF definition, what SPECIAL privilege does an SSF have?

answer.text: SSF has no special IBC privileges.
SSF can act as a Resolution Applicant under the IBC, 2016, in accordance with its investment objectives — a privilege specifically recognised in the Chapter 9 SSF definition.
SSF can only participate in liquidation, never in resolution.
SSF must mandatorily exit before IBC admission of any investee.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 defines a Special Situation Fund as a Category I AIF that invests in special situation assets in accordance with its investment objectives, and it may act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016. This is the SSF's recognised regulatory accommodation that allows it to bid as a Resolution Applicant. The Trap: Options A, C, and D strip out the specific RA privilege. The ability to act as a Resolution Applicant under IBC, 2016, is the differentiator that the workbook explicitly attaches to SSFs. Note: Anchor any SSF-as-RA exam answer to the precise workbook language about acting as a resolution applicant in accordance with its investment objectives.
